key_insight: TASK memory reduces hallucinations even when the correct memory is already retrieved by controlling whether an LLM uses external memory or its own knowledge.
engineering_relevance: Memory-enabled agents may need query-specific control over memory use, not just better retrieval, to avoid stale answers and applying facts to unrelated entities.
method: Store factual content in a text note.
Use a removable knowledge edit to provide a shared in-model address and support multi-hop composition.
Apply paired, content-free steering vectors to control memory adoption for each query.
evidence_signal: Under a pre-registered, test-once protocol across five open models, TASK reduced memory-ignoring to ≤1.5% in all 10 model–dataset cells and improved a 300-memory library by 16.4 percentage points over BM25 RAG.
watch_item: Deployment requires access to model activations and editable weights; the abstract does not establish latency or maintenance costs for larger memory libraries.
paper_title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
